parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a black-box Rust 2021 port of test2.cpp requiring std-only modules, root /output/test2.rs, Cargo structure, exact C++ CLI parsing, byte-identical stdout, and no earcut.hpp source reading.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent split work by spawning a probe child and a design child; the design child returned recommendations, the probe child spawned a nested probe and also began implementing, while the parent retained final implementation and verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Parent implemented a test2_port Cargo project with atoi, polygon, render, and triangulation modules that matched observed square and hole index sequences; the probe child independently wrote a competing Cargo project with cli, geometry, and triangulation modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent's files became the active root deliverable and were compiled; extra child files and build products remained in the artifact but were not wired into the final parent Cargo.toml path used by the passing solution.
parallel.verification: Parent ran cargo test, rustc, cargo build --release, and a side-by-side comparison against /workspace/dataset/test2_executable for no-arg, normal, malformed, signed, fractional, and overflow arguments.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official result passed 40 of 40; the remaining defect is process-level only: the child implementation branch was superseded during shared workspace use and left inert extra files.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same black-box port requirements: std-only Rust 2021, /output/test2.rs, Cargo project, std::env::args parsing, C-style atoi behavior, and exact stdout including trailing spaces and no newline.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned discovery, implementation, integration, cleanup, and verification end to end with no child delegation and no shared ownership boundary.
serial.implementation: Implemented a single Cargo project with cli, geometry, lib, triangulation, and root test2.rs files, including explicit C-style atoi behavior and fixed triangulation behavior for the exercised shapes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Started with an empty /output, wrote one coherent project, removed a warning-causing re-export, rebuilt, and delivered the expected root entry and Cargo package without stray sibling implementation files.
serial.verification: Ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc --edition=2021 /output/test2.rs -o /output/test2, then compared output against the C++ executable across examples, negatives, whitespace, malformed strings, and overflow-style values.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved implementation defect is visible in trajectory or official evaluation; current official evaluator passed all 40 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized exact CLI/output behavior, std-only Rust, Cargo project layout, root test2.rs, and black-box implementation constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and translated them into a single-agent black-box port plan.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap explains outcome; both passed all official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split probing and design into child agents while the parent also kept implementation and final verification; the probe child expanded into nested probing and then independent implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one owner for discovery, implementation, integration, testing, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced overlapping implementation ownership in /output; serial avoided that coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received design guidance and nested probe findings, but no visible file-ownership interface kept the probe child from writing the same deliverable surface the parent later wrote.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface; the same actor consumed its own probing output and implemented directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The context/interface difference was shared ownership of /output in parallel, not a missing task fact in serial or a failed handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent built a modular port around observed outputs, while the probe child separately wrote an alternative project in the same /output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one modular project after probing behavior and did not merge alternative implementations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both final implementations matched the task, but parallel's implementation path included a competing child project later superseded by the parent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent received and used design/probe information, then interrupted the still-running probe child only after the parent had already built and verified a passing solution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve or join and closed after its own verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra child lifecycle handling, including an interrupt of unneeded remaining child work; serial had no comparable result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Probe child and parent both wrote /output project deliverables; child reconciliation later failed against changed files and parent noticed extra child-created source files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial started with empty /output and wrote a single coherent project with no concurrent writer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the concrete parallel-specific coordination defect: shared deliverable overwrite and residual inert files, though official evaluation still passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent ran unit tests, rustc, release build, and output comparisons against the C++ executable before finalizing; official evaluation also passed 40 of 40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc, and many output comparisons before finalizing; official evaluation also passed 40 of 40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification was sufficient in both runs; serial's output comparison covered more malformed/whitespace cases, but the official outcome did not diverge.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four rollout files, 67 tool calls, 714192 total tokens, and 218.575 agent seconds, with no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout file, 23 tool calls, 289771 total tokens, and 177.41 agent seconds, with no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more coordination and token budget, but still closed with verified passing work; the budget difference is not itself a retained load imbalance.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed: the parallel and serial attempts each implemented the required std-only Rust port, built the root test2.rs/Cargo project, and verified representative executable behavior. The parallel run differed by introducing overlapping child and parent writes in /output, but the parent ultimately delivered and verified a passing implementation, so the retained pattern is a process defect rather than an outcome differential.
parallel_contributors: Parent independently built and verified the final deliverable after using or duplicating child probing/design information.
A probe child wrote a competing project in the same /output tree, but the parent superseded it and still passed.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained ownership of probing, implementation, cleanup, and verification.
Serial compared many representative outputs and passed the same official 40 of 40 evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial used a single c_atoi/render-output implementation with broader explicit comparison cases; parallel used separate atoi/polygon/render/triangulation modules in the final parent project.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process episode, not a scoring differential

candidates.reason: The parent and probe child both implemented rather than leaving implementation ownerless.
The parent owned final integration and verification; the defect was conflicting writes, not absent integration ownership.
The parent assembled the root test2.rs Cargo deliverable and built it successfully.
The parent owned the end-to-end build, comparison, and final response despite child activity.
Parent implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; it probed and implemented while children ran.
Investigation and implementation overlapped, and later work was not left incomplete or underverified by an investigation phase.
The critical implementation path had enough parent capacity and passed; no indispensable task path was starved.
Although parallel used more tokens and children, it did not exhaust deadline or budget and official evaluation passed.
No single delegated child scope is proven overbroad from visible brief text; the adverse episode is a write collision.
The child briefs are encrypted and there is no direct evidence that a known requirement was omitted and followed to failure.
A file ownership contract may have helped, but the directly observed event is concrete deliverable overwrite, which takes precedence.
No known finding is shown before transfer and then absent after transfer; parent had enough behavior evidence to pass.
Returned child information was not shown to be too large or unconsumed within the decision window.
No receiver acted on a superseded handoff; the stale state was the child's on-disk workspace after overwrite, not a transferred report.
No incompatible reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated; the conflict was concrete file state.
Parent performed integrated cargo/rustc/output checks before final response; no visible acceptance gap remained.
There was no replacement or retry episode that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent interrupted the probe child after parent verification; no still-needed child result was stopped before finalization.
A complete promotable candidate was finalized and verified in time; the child branch was not needed for delivery.
Parent did not integrate child result after verification; its own verified files remained the active deliverable.
The child implementation was superseded before becoming the needed completed implementation; the direct issue is overwrite, not unjoined finished work.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent before closure.
No required child failure was left untaken over; parent independently completed and verified the final solution.
The visible design result was received and consistent with the parent path; no available completed result was ignored to the detriment of the task.
A short wait timed out, but the parent continued active implementation and verification rather than idling until deadline.
The episode went beyond cross-file competing design: the required deliverable files themselves were overwritten.
Same-file collision is less specific because the same files included the root deliverable and Cargo project surface.
Library source files were also affected, but deliverable overwrite has higher precedence for the root entrypoint/project.
Probe child wrote the required /output project and root entrypoint, then the parent wrote its own required project over that deliverable surface while the child was still active.
candidates.realized_consequence: The child's follow-up patch failed against changed files and the final artifact contained residual child files/build products, requiring parent inspection even though the final solution passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is present as a symptom, but the overwritten files included the required entrypoint/submitted project deliverable, so the more specific deliverable label applies.

candidates.reason: There was no broad cleanup or final-tree promotion replacing multiple finalized outputs; the direct overwrite was the project deliverable surface.
Shared workspace writing occurred, but the more specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven and takes precedence.
Extra child files remained, but no actor consumed a generated artifact as a false reference environment or stable input.

retained_patterns.reason: A live probe child wrote a root /output project and later attempted to continue modifying it after the parent independently wrote a different project over the same required deliverable surface.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The child's in-progress implementation branch became unusable against the changed on-disk project, and the parent had to inspect unexpected residual child files before finalizing.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-file collision describes part of the collision, but taxonomy precedence chooses Deliverable Overwrite because the root entrypoint and Cargo deliverable surface were replaced.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision and Source Overwrite are suppressed for the same shared-output chain because Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.
Unisolated Workspace Writes is suppressed because the concrete deliverable overwrite is proven.
Early Child Termination and Missing Implementation Join are rejected as downstream symptoms of an unneeded child branch after parent verification.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the directly evidenced shared deliverable overwrite cleared the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were added for child count, higher token use, harmless waiting, unused inert files alone, or passing evaluator status.
